claim: Noise filtering runs through the packaged FFmpeg helper — the afftdn filter and the wav muxer the clean-up writes through — and the denoise measurement passes in the hosted Linux, macOS and Windows jobs.

verification.detail: The three native jobs build the helper with the pinned configure line and run scripts/measure_denoise.py against it; the Rust job runs the audio-cleanup unit tests. The helper is built --disable-everything with the afftdn filter and the wav muxer added deliberately.

limitations: The measurement uses synthetic PCM (white noise plus a tone), not recorded speech; it establishes the filter chain and the container, not perceptual quality on real material.

The loudness numbers (an 11.5 dB floor drop with 11.3 dB of discrimination, and a derived -21 dBFS floor) are local developer measurements; the hosted jobs verify that the measurement passes, not those exact values on every platform.
Voice enhancement and loudness normalisation are not covered by this record.
